narr: Tropical Depression 28 over the western Caribbean, which eventually became Hurricane Zeta, helped to provide copious tropical moisture over South Florida. As an upper level trough traversed aloft, additional deep moisture overspread the South Florida ahead of an approaching frontal boundary. This resulted in widespread rainfall over several days that lead to significant flooding across the east coast metro areas, which had already received several inches of rainfall from previous days. ||The most impactful flooding occurred in Palm Beach County where several neighborhoods across the county experienced major street and field flooding, and several homes had water intrusion. The flooding lingered for several days in some of these areas.
ev: Significant flooding occurred in the Sea Pines neighborhood of Lantana resulting from a combination of heavy rainfall of the previous days plus 4-5 inches of rain on the night and early morning of October 24th and 25th. Numerous calls were received from residents stranded in their homes, some who had water in their homes up to their knees. Streets were impassable across the entire neighborhood. Flood waters lingered for several days in the area (this is detailed in a separate storm entry under Flood).

Significant flooding occurred in the Lake Boynton Estates area of Boynton Beach, resulting from a combination of heavy rainfall of the previous days plus 4-5 inches of rain on the night and early morning of October 24th and 25th. Two to three homes had water intrusion, and water was about 2 feet deep on streets. Four families in the area requested to be evacuated. Flood waters lingered for over 24 hours (this is detailed in a separate storm entry under Flood).
